title: FLF BREAKS DNA
description:
A Collection of Their Most Classic and Wildest Pioneering Experimental Breakbeat Tracks — Full-Length & Remastered**

London-based breakbeat trio Friends, Lovers & Family have long occupied a fringe yet influential corner of electronic music: techno art-house, early breakbeat and sample-driven mayhem, where the machines hum and the rhythm fractures.

With *FLF Breaks DNA*, the band digs deep into this legacy. The album is described as a full-length remastered collection of their earliest, wildest breakbeat experiments—tracks that once melted dancefloor subwoofers, cracked DJ sets, and pushed the boundaries of rhythm in the mid-90s and beyond.

Friends, Lovers & Family were experimenting at a time when breakbeat was still a subterranean language. Their work blends raw beats, fragments of funk, techno minimalism and stubby sample chops, placing them ahead of many peers.

This new edition offers restored clarity, punch and fidelity—so the shards of broken rhythm shine in modern playback.

Rather than a mere EP or “best of”, the collection is full-length—meaning you’re getting the experience in one expansive sequence. You’re invited not just to hear a track, but to immerse in the breakbeat world they built.

Jagged rhythms, heavy sub-bass, chopped break-beats that stutter and reset, layered with minimal keys or sneaky vocal samples. It’s less stable groove and more kinetic shock—these are tracks designed to unsettle and energise. The remastering gives them shine and weight without losing the raw edges.

There will also be moments of reflection—echoes of the techno art-house heritage the band cite. Interludes or stripped-down passages may emerge amid the beat collapse, making the listening journey more than a DJ set: it becomes a sound-world.

In a time when breakbeat is revisited, re-interpreted and sometimes diluted, *FLF Breaks DNA* stands as a document—an original blueprint. Friends, Lovers & Family are not riding trends, they *helped build* one. 

For fans of heavier rhythm, for those curious about the underground veins of UK electronic music, this collection is both historical and immediate. You can hear where things *came from* and how that energy still sounds fresh.

These beats mattered. They still matter. And in their remastered form, they roar back with full power. If you’ve ever wondered how breakbeat could be shaped, sculpted and shattered into something art-house, Friends, Lovers & Family deliver. Plug in, strap in, and let the fractured rhythms take you somewhere wild.

title: Ordinary People Original and Alternate Mixes Remastered 2025
SECRET LAB
description:
A collection of early experimental breakbeat 1992-1994

Friends, Lovers & Family are a pioneering techno art-house breakbeat trio whose work sits at the fractured edge of electronic music. Formed over 30 years ago, their sound emerged from the underground where broken rhythms, raw machines, and experimental instinct collided — long before breakbeat became a genre with rules.

Drawing from techno, early rave, industrial textures and cut-up funk, FLF built tracks that were as much about tension and atmosphere as dancefloor impact. Their music resists polish, favouring grit, space, and rhythm that bends and mutates rather than settles.

Across released material, unreleased archives, and long-buried DAT recordings, Friends, Lovers & Family document a restless creative spirit — one that treats electronic music as process, experiment, and emotional transmission. Their work feels both of its time and strangely outside it: a reminder of when machines were explored, not domesticated.

Now revisited and remastered, their catalogue stands as a vital snapshot of early experimental breakbeat culture — uncompromising, forward-thinking, and deeply human beneath the circuitry.
